propositions: An errored pair with synthetic decision is incorrectly scored as a decision flip because parity.py:107 compares decisions with no errored guard, violating the documented contract that errored records are not model verdicts.

A single transient runtime error (e.g. throttle) on one arm fails the parity gate criterion (b) by counting as a decision flip, causing false model-quality regression signals when no actual model behavior changed.

The flip gating criterion double-counts the same event under both criterion (b) decision-flip and criterion (d) error-rate checks, and the report cannot distinguish fabricated flips from real ones because errored_pairs is not surfaced separately.

An errored record with errored=True and valid=True produces a silent, undetectable fabricated flip because the synthetic decision differs from the other arm's verdict while validity appears unchanged.

The fix excludes gold pairs where either side has errored=True from decision_flips computation, counts them into a new errored_pairs metric, and surfaces it in ParityReport.metrics and gating failure strings to distinguish arms with real vs. fabricated flips.
